_metadata.independence: I read only x12-rd-input.json and judged each hint on its merits, without opening any other file, searching the repository or using the web.

hints.reason: APPLE via the apple core and EARTH via the planet's core; a clean, instantly fair shared property.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, easy clue; no better single word.

hints.reason: BAND via going on tour and BUS via the tour bus; one coherent scene that clicks at once.

pairs.pair_note: Natural, easy pairing.

hints.reason: BAND via Toto, the band behind "Africa," and DOG via Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz; two famous, unrelated referents for one name, a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch; both facts are accurate.

hints.reason: FAN via a groupie being a devoted fan and BAND via groupies following bands; close to a definition, but a specific word, not a plain synonym of FAN, and it points squarely at both.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair. Groupie has a mild rock-culture connotation but is an everyday PG word; the text keeps it innocent.

hints.reason: BAND via the Eagles as a classic rock band and HOTEL via their signature song "Hotel California"; an indirect route with a good click.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect band clue; the song is widely known.

hints.reason: PEPPER via Sgt. Pepper and BAND via the album title ending "Lonely Hearts Club Band"; one famous title covers both, and SERGEANT is an unexpected word that lands.

pairs.pair_note: The spelled-out SERGEANT is fine for the "Sgt." title. Lines are accurate.

hints.reason: BAND and ROSE both via the band name Guns N' Roses; a phrase-join, but the name is instantly familiar and GUNS on its own points nowhere else on a board like this.

pairs.pair_note: Plain phrase-join that still passes on familiarity. SLASH (the guitarist) is a more indirect alternative but less broadly known; not clearly better.

hints.reason: BAND via the drummer's drumsticks and TURKEY via the turkey leg; a clean double meaning with a real "oh, nice" moment.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; DRIVER-style double meaning.

hints.reason: BAND via the Doors, the classic rock band, and WINDOW via doors and windows as the paired openings of a house; the window side is a sibling association rather than an identity, but it is a very strong pair and clicks at once.

pairs.pair_note: The WINDOW side is the softer one (other words could share it), but per the DRIVER calibration that alone is not a reason to fail.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the St. Louis Cardinals and CHURCH via a cardinal as a senior Catholic official; a satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; both facts accurate.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the baseball diamond and RING via the diamond in an engagement ring; a classic, clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong and easy.

hints.reason: BEACH via surfing the waves and INTERNET via surfing the web; a familiar double meaning, easy but satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: "Surf the web" is a little dated but still universally understood.

hints.reason: BIRD via the long-legged crane and BUILDING via the construction crane; a neat double meaning (the machine is even named after the bird).

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: BOWLING via a strike knocking down all ten pins and MATCH via striking a match; a clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; MATCH could also be read as a sports match, which gives a nice misdirection.

hints.reason: BRIDGE via the troll under the bridge in "Three Billy Goats Gruff" and INTERNET via online trolls; folklore meets modern slang, a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; facts accurate.

hints.reason: CANDY and VIDEO GAME both via the title Candy Crush, the famous mobile game; a phrase-join, but the title is instantly familiar and the game side is not a mere blank-fill.

pairs.pair_note: Note: CRUSH is also the hint for p_love__orange in this batch; avoid serving both close together.

hints.reason: CARD via the four card suits and COURT via a lawsuit (a "suit") going to court; a good double meaning that needs one small step on the court side.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. Players may also try the court-card/face-card route, which is a pleasant red herring.

hints.reason: CARD via the ace playing card and TENNIS via an ace serve; a well-known double meaning. The tennis wording is slightly loose: an ace is a serve the receiver cannot touch, not any unreturned serve.
hints.fix: In tennis, an ace is a serve the opponent can't even touch.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and fair; the text fix is minor precision only.

hints.reason: CAT via Garfield the cartoon cat and LAZY via his famous laziness; an easy, obvious, satisfying character clue.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but excellent fit.

hints.reason: CEREAL via Trix cereal and RABBIT via the Trix rabbit mascot ("Silly rabbit..."); a classic mascot clue with a nostalgic click.

pairs.pair_note: Cereal mascots are explicitly in scope; strong.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via the Snickers bar and LAUGH via a snicker being a sly laugh; brand plus everyday word, a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. (Chuckles candy would be another route, but Snickers is far better known.)

hints.reason: CODE via the Java programming language and COFFEE via "java" as slang for coffee; a well-known double meaning with a satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; both lines accurate.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via saving a file and SOCCER via a goalkeeper's save; a clean, everyday double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: DEER via Rudolph being a reindeer (reindeer are deer) and RED via his red nose; instantly familiar. The explanation is only the song title and does not state the link.
hints.fix: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer is a deer with a shining red nose.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair holiday clue; facts accurate (reindeer belong to the deer family).

hints.reason: SNOWMAN via Olaf being a snowman and DISNEY via Frozen; an easy, exact character fit.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean.

hints.reason: DONKEY and VIDEO GAME both via the classic arcade game Donkey Kong; a phrase-join (KONG may first suggest King Kong) but the title is instantly familiar. The DONKEY line wrongly implies the ape's name is just "Donkey."
hints.fix: The game's giant ape is called Donkey Kong.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on familiarity; fix the DONKEY line, since the character's name is Donkey Kong, not "Donkey."

hints.reason: ENGLAND via the English Channel and TELEVISION via TV channels; geography plus everyday tech, a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the English Channel fact is correct.

hints.reason: EYE via the eye socket gives the aha, but OUTLET is reached only because socket is essentially a synonym for an electrical outlet (the line even says "An outlet is a socket"); a strict reading of the synonym rule could fail it, while the eye side makes it feel like a fair double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Uncertain call worth a second opinion: SOCKET is the natural hint for this pair and plays well, but one side is a near-synonym of the target. No clearly better single word.

hints.reason: FISH via sole the flatfish and SHOE via the sole of a shoe; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: FOOTBALL via the Miami Dolphins and OCEAN via dolphins swimming in the sea; a familiar team-plus-animal clue.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and easy; sports teams are in scope.

hints.reason: GARDEN via moles tunnelling through gardens and SPY via a mole as an infiltrator; a satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; both lines accurate.

hints.reason: HAIR via the bun hairstyle and HAMBURGER via the burger bun; a neat, everyday double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: HEEL via the Achilles heel and HERO via Achilles the Greek hero; the idiom is universal and the hero side adds a small aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the weak-heel detail is the standard legend.

hints.reason: LOVE via having a crush and ORANGE via Orange Crush soda; a brand-plus-feeling double meaning that clicks.

pairs.pair_note: Good. CRUSH also serves p_candy__video-game; space them apart.

hints.reason: VIDEO GAME via the Pokemon series and MONSTER via the name coming from "Pocket Monsters"; a true origin fact that gives a RELATIVE-style aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the Pocket Monsters origin is accurate and fairly well known, and Pokemon read as monsters even without it.

hints.reason: MUSIC via pop music and SODA via "pop" as a word for soda; a fair, familiar double meaning. The SODA line overstates a regional usage as universal.
hints.fix: In many parts of the U.S., soda is called pop.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; soda-vs-pop regional debate is itself a well-known bit of U.S. culture.

hints.reason: PHONE via the Samsung Galaxy and SPACE via galaxies; a brand-plus-science double meaning, easy but satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; "huge star system" is loose but acceptable wording for a galaxy.

hints.reason: VIDEO GAME via Mario as the iconic game hero and PIPE via his green warp pipes (and his job as a plumber); an indirect, satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the plumber angle doubles the PIPE link.

hints.reason: PRINCESS via Ariel the Disney princess and SEA via her life "under the sea"; an easy, exact character fit.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean; facts accurate.

hints.reason: VIDEO GAME via the game controller is strong, but REMOTE comes only via a remote being a kind of controller, a near-definitional and flat link; WII (whose controller is literally the Wii Remote) hits both with a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Swap to WII: the Wii Remote is a widely known video game controller, giving both sides through one familiar product.

hints.reason: SPACE and VIDEO GAME both via the classic arcade game Space Invaders; a phrase-join, but the title is instantly familiar and the alien-invaders-from-space reading adds a little texture.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on familiarity; classic arcade games are in scope.

hints.reason: VIDEO GAME via Pong as one of the first hit video games and TENNIS via Pong being a simple table-tennis (ping-pong) game; a satisfying indirect link.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; both facts accurate.
